# Optional first-boot preferences and development recovery access.
# Normal setup needs NO card edits: connect HDMI and Ethernet, or use a USB
# keyboard for Wi-Fi. Open the URL/QR code on HDMI. First setup needs no password.
# The image initializes its factory-empty data automatically. Established and
# imported data is never replaced. Only legacy EMPTY labelled data needs:
# initialize_data=yes
# New installations use login-free home-LAN management. An optional password
# protects management after setup (username satip), or set one later in Settings:
# setup_password=your-browser-password
# lan_access=authenticated
# Explicit login-free management, including device settings: lan_access=login-free
# timezone=Europe/Berlin
# drm_connector=HDMI-A-2
# drm_mode=1920x1080@50
# audio_device=alsa/hdmi:CARD=vc4hdmi1,DEV=0
# USB keyboards and GPIO infrared are always enabled together.
# Optional additional USB remote identity (also selectable in the browser):
# keyboard_vendor=04d9
# keyboard_product=0006
# ir_profile=apple-a1294
# Legacy ir_profile=disabled remains parseable; infrared now stays enabled.
# Optional server description; otherwise automatic home-network discovery:
# satip_xml=http://192.168.1.10/desc.xml
# satellite=Astra-19.2E
# satip_source=1
# Optional tuner preference; the browser can select any available frontend:
# tuner_number=2
# Never put real values in source/build inputs. Edit only the flashed card.
# Literal key=value, no shell expansion, quoting or inline comments.
hostname=satip-dev
# Optional SSH access, independent of browser access. Login username: root.
# ssh_enabled=yes
# The Pi hashes a supplied root password internally. Recovery settings can also
# be changed through this file on later boots.
# root_password=your-root-password
# Optional existing-key access:
# ssh_authorized_key=ssh-ed25519 AAAA...
# Optional WPA/WPA2 Personal Wi-Fi. Country, SSID and PSK go together.
# UTF-8 SSIDs and printable ASCII passwords; spaces in both are preserved.
# wifi_country=DE
# wifi_ssid=your-network
# wifi_psk=your-private-passphrase
# After successful first-boot import this file is automatically restored from
# the image template. Settings persist on data. This is not secure flash erasure.
